title: Exercise during pregnancy

Avoid activities where you could fall or be hit in the belly, and stop and rest if you feel pain, dizziness, bleeding or are very short of breath. Ask your health worker what is safe for you.

If you feel extremely tired, weak or breathless all the time, tell a health worker, as it can be a sign of anaemia.

A pillow or folded cloth between your knees or behind your back can make side sleeping more comfortable. If you wake up on your back, just turn onto your side.

title: Constipation in pregnancy
answer: Constipation, meaning hard or infrequent stools, is common in pregnancy because hormones slow the gut, and iron tablets can add to it. If it lasts or is very painful, or you see blood, talk to a health worker rather than buying laxatives.

title: Danger signs in a newborn
answer: Take your baby to a health facility immediately if the baby: is not feeding well or stops breastfeeding; has fits; breathes fast or with difficulty, or the chest pulls in; feels hot (fever) or too cold; moves only when touched or not at all; has yellow skin in the first day or yellow palms and soles; or has redness, pus or a bad smell around the cord. Newborns can get very sick quickly, so do not wait. Call 912 for an ambulance if needed.

title: Healthy birth spacing
answer: After having a baby, WHO advises waiting at least 24 months (two years) before trying to get pregnant again. Spacing births gives your body time to recover and rebuild its strength, and lowers the risk of problems like early birth, low birth weight and anaemia for the next baby. It also gives you time to care for your baby, finish school or work. A health worker can help you choose a family planning method that suits you, including while breastfeeding.
